# E0507: failures passed on without their error type

This would take your caller's failures for an error of its own type. Write `raise<E>` in the parameter's row, so that callers pass only those.

- Rule: [`effects.passing-to-paired-variables`](../../reference/12-effects.md#effects.passing-to-paired-variables)
- Reported at: the use of the function: the call, or its name taken as a value.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `analyses` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0507:3
type Box = { v: i64 }

fn wrap(g: fn() -> i64) -> Result<i64, Box> { Result.of(g) }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
type Box = { v: i64 }

fn wrap(g: fn() -> i64 / raise<Box>) -> Result<i64, Box> { Result.of(g) }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0507_failures_passed_on_without_their_error_type.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0507_failures_passed_on_without_their_error_type.lt):

```text
── FAILURES PASSED ON WITHOUT THEIR ERROR TYPE ── E0507_failures_passed_on_without_their_error_type.lt:3:47  [E0507]

This takes `g`'s failures for a `Box`, but they belong to the caller:

  3 │ fn wrap(g: fn() -> i64) -> Result<i64, Box> { Result.of(g) }
    │                                               ^^^^^^^^^

This would take your caller's failures for an error of its own type. Write
`raise<E>` in the parameter's row, so that callers pass only those.

To fix it, say that `g` raises `Box`: write `raise<Box>` in its row:

  3 │ fn wrap(g: fn() -> i64 / raise<Box>) -> Result<i64, Box> { Result.of(g) }
    │                       +++++++++++++
```
